cells.tense: Right now, you can say the shape of a thing and have the saying hold it.
cells.act: let several things be true and act on one
cells.ask: Where more than one thing is true at once, name each to yourself in plain order, then move on just one and leave the others true and untouched for now.
cells.core:
You can say what you see and have it land. In a group, or alone in your own head, you can hold several true things at once without one swallowing the others, then move on the one that matters today. Flow holds because you keep sensing what to add and what to leave be.

Take one spot where more than one thing is true — a decision, a plan, a read on a person — and lay all of them out in plain order before you move. Then move on one, and leave the others true. The picture doesn't have to collapse for the step to be single. What you know stays wide, what you do stays small, and nothing true gets dropped to make it neat.
cells.sheetLine: You can say what you see, and it holds.
cells.verb: declares a structure outward and claims the ground it stands on
cells.place: in the ongoing adjustment that keeps a blend at flow

cells.tense: Soon, every situation is being described before it has had a chance to show itself to you.
cells.act: go all the way into the pattern until you meet its edge
cells.ask: Take a problem you've already filed as solved and follow it past the first clean answer, into the part that won't resolve — stay until you reach the edge of what you can name.
cells.core:
You've been naming things fast, and the names run past the situations. A shape gets described, and the description shuts the question before it opened. From outside it reads as clarity — clean, decisive — and it keeps you from being shown anything you didn't already organize. The very skill you have at adjusting jumps straight to the end state, and the blend pays for it.

Take something you've already filed as solved and follow it in past the first clean answer, into the part that won't resolve. Stay until you hit the edge. The edge is where your mind can't name anything, and it's where the situation finally gets to talk back. What's there is worth more than this morning's clean description, and the only price is staying.

cells.tense: For a while now, the claim that used to come easily is not being made.
cells.act: keep building the thing with sustained craft
cells.ask: Go back to the project you set down and give it one real hour today, until a piece sits more solid than before, then return tomorrow the same way.
cells.core:
There's a door behind you, and you're still at it. The old build stalled or got dropped, and since then the saying has gone quiet — you see the shape of things and don't name it, don't claim it, don't lay the next piece. Your ease is being kept by not entering the game. From outside it looks calm. Inside, the ground you used to take is going ungrown.

Go back to the project you set down and work it for one real hour — the kind where a piece gets more solid before you stop. Then come back tomorrow. The commitment is small and physical, and it teaches the hands what the head already knows: a thing becomes real by being built daily. By the third or fourth day the dialogue resumes, and the door behind you closes by being walked past.

cells.tense: In the middle of give and take, the structure under the blend is being held by you, unclaimed.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: Some ending has already happened here — a way of doing things, a shape a relationship took. Set down two things it grew that are still with you, counted as yours.
cells.core:
The blend you keep at flow is held together by structure you lay and don't sign. You adjust, you sense what to add and take away, and you talk as though the arrangement were simply how things are. The back-and-forth you're so good at rests on decisions you made and didn't claim. Even you don't count them as yours.

The earlier form of that same line is simpler: you used to name the endings and tally what they grew. Think of one ending that has already happened here — a way of doing things, a shape a relationship took — and set down two things it grew that are still with you. The tally puts the pen back in your hand. What looked like the room's own shape turns out to be your work, and you can sign it.
cells.sheetLine: The structure under your blend is held by you, unsigned.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person experiences the act as 'dynamic equilibrium / Tune' in any felt way — the record only places the seat as the domain of the adjustment. The reader could reasonably say the seat is my label, not their experience. The asks survive being wrong: each is one visible act in the world of blend-and-adjust, useful whether or not they agree with the read. The sentence that serves me is 'things make sense in your presence' — it flatters rather than locates, so it is kept out of every cell.
